assertion_results.text: For each task created, a description digest is produced — evidenced by a separate digest file (e.g., task-N-digest.md), a digest entry in the impact map, or a '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-char-hex>' marker in any output file. The digest must contain a format-tagged SHA-256 hash — exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed by 'sha256-md:' or 'sha256-adf:'
assertion_results.evidence: All 8 digest files (task-1-digest.md through task-8-digest.md) exist but contain placeholder text: '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<computed-after-jira-persistence>'. The value '<computed-after-jira-persistence>' is not 64 lowercase hex characters — it is a placeholder explanation. The assertion requires 'exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed by sha256-md: or sha256-adf:', which is not satisfied by any digest file.

assertion_results.text: Convention-aware enrichment validates file-type applicability per shared/convention-applicability-rules.md before including a convention — inapplicable conventions are excluded entirely (not listed with 'Not applicable' annotations), and applicable ones include a rationale in the prescribed format ('Applies: task modifies <file> matching the convention's <scope>'), not free-form prose
assertion_results.evidence: Tasks 1-5 include convention references in free-form prose format ('Per repo conventions: all handlers return Result<T, AppError> with .context() wrapping', 'Per repo conventions: integration tests in tests/api/ use the assert_eq! pattern'). None of these follow the prescribed rationale format 'Applies: task modifies <file> matching the convention's <scope>'. No instance of the string 'Applies:' or the prescribed format appears anywhere in the output files. The convention-applicability-rules.md requires this exact format and prohibits free-form prose rationales.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: Feature TC-9001 has priority 'Major'. The impact-map.md Jira Field Inheritance section states: 'Priority: Major (inherited from TC-9001)' and includes JSON: '"priority": {"name": "Major"}'. The summary-comment.md states: 'Priority: Major — propagated to all Epics and Tasks (Feature priority is "Major", not "Undefined")'.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: Feature TC-9001 has fixVersions 'RHTPA 1.5.0'. No fixVersion scope config exists in CLAUDE.md (defaults to 'both'). The impact-map.md states: 'Fix Versions: RHTPA 1.5.0 (inherited from TC-9001; no fixVersion scope setting found in Jira Configuration, defaulting to "both" — propagate to tasks)' and includes JSON: '"fixVersions": [{"name": "RHTPA 1.5.0"}]'. The summary-comment.md confirms: 'Fix Versions: RHTPA 1.5.0 — propagated to all Epics and Tasks'.

assertion_results.text: A summary of inherited field propagation is produced — evidenced by a summary-comment.md file in the outputs directory, or a summary section in the impact map that includes the inherited priority and fixVersion values propagated to tasks, or states they were omitted and why
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md exists at /tmp/plan-feature-eval-baseline/eval-1/outputs/summary-comment.md with an 'Inherited Field Values' section stating: 'Priority: Major — propagated to all Epics and Tasks', 'Fix Versions: RHTPA 1.5.0 — propagated to all Epics and Tasks', and 'Labels: ["ai-generated-jira"] — applied to all created issues'.
